phase10_downstream_feasibility.exclusion_test: cell 309 is EXCLUDED iff the certified floor on E_a[tau] exceeds the critical A0
phase10_downstream_feasibility.interpretation: C4's exclusion tolerated a 0.94% adverse move in the critical A0. A single successor, C5-T, had already consumed 63% of C4's original margin. Under C7's PRIMARY bound the exclusion tolerates 9.7933%, so a C5-T-sized move no longer threatens it. This is a statement about the ROBUSTNESS of an existing exclusion, not a new closure.
phase10_downstream_feasibility.scope: FEASIBILITY_ONLY -- no cell status changes, no closure is claimed, guard stays DENY

phase11_family_exhaustion.ceiling_derivation: (H + sup provable E[R]) / E[V], with E[R] at Lorden's upper bound. No choice of partition, split points or U can exceed this, because it is what the family yields when E[R] is known exactly at its largest provable value.
phase11_family_exhaustion.conclusion: The E2 family CANNOT reach the certified operator constant A0 = 4.867216117, so it can never make the cell-309 blocker vanish on its own. It does not need to: the exclusion test is against the critical A0, which it clears by 9.7933%. The remaining headroom inside the family is the gap between the primary bound and the ceiling, i.e. up to 30.4939% more, obtainable only by sharpening the lower bound on E[R] toward its true value.
phase11_family_exhaustion.family: E2 -- overshoot corrections to the C4 bound H/E[V] using only the increment law
